seoTitle: How to Add a Dynamic Dropdown to Jotform
metaDescription: Learn how to build cascading, dependent dropdown menus in Jotform in 2026 using the Dynamic Dropdowns widget for parent-child selections.
intro: A single flat dropdown gets messy fast once you're dealing with categories that have sub-options, and Jotform's Dynamic Dropdowns widget solves that with cascading parent-child menus. This guide covers adding the widget, formatting nested choices, and testing that secondary lists update correctly based on earlier selections.

steps.heading: Open the Widgets tab
steps.body: In your form builder, open the Add Form Element sidebar and switch to the Widgets tab to search for Dynamic Dropdowns.

steps.heading: Add the widget to your form
steps.body: Drag the Dynamic Dropdowns element onto your form layout.

steps.heading: Open the widget settings
steps.body: Launch the Widget Settings panel to begin configuring your data menu.

steps.heading: Format nested parent-child options
steps.body: Use indented values to build dependent menus so secondary lists update based on the parent selection.

steps.heading: Adjust labels and test the cascade
steps.body: Set label names, placeholders, and separator symbols, then test the live form to confirm cascading selections work smoothly on desktop and mobile.

faq.question: How many levels of nested dropdowns can I create?
faq.answer: The widget supports multi-level nesting through indentation, so you can build several tiers of parent-child options depending on your data structure.

faq.question: Do I need coding knowledge to set up dynamic dropdowns?
faq.answer: No, the widget is configured through indented text values in the settings panel rather than any custom code.

faq.question: Can I use dynamic dropdowns for location-based selections?
faq.answer: Yes, cascading dropdowns are commonly used for things like country, state, and city selections that depend on each other.

faq.question: Why isn't my child dropdown updating when I change the parent?
faq.answer: This is usually caused by incorrect indentation in the nested values, so double-check that child options are properly indented under the right parent choice.
